profile.campus: Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster (SFO1-SFO4, formerly Centersquare, formerly Evoque Data Center Solutions)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
This building, which Csquare markets as SFO3, sits at 1400 Kifer Road in Sunnyvale, California, part of Csquare's four building Silicon Valley cluster. Unlike SFO1 and SFO4 elsewhere in that cluster, which each span two separate buildings, Csquare's own SEC registration prospectus lists a single rentable unit under the SFO3 code, SFO3_A, leased rather than company owned, at 19,958 rentable square feet and 82.8 percent occupied as of March 31, 2026, giving this record an unusually clean one to one match between the OpenStreetMap building and the company's own property table. Csquare's separate facility page for SFO3 puts the raised floor area slightly lower, at 19,661 square feet, a routine difference between a leasing measure and a raised floor measure rather than a contradiction, and states that this single building draws 8.6 megawatts of utility power, runs 3.2 megawatts of UPS protected capacity, and backs up on 5 megawatts of generator capacity, certified to SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High and ISO 27001 standards plus ENERGY STAR, with four carrier neutral service providers on site. Because SFO3 is a single building code rather than a two building pair like its siblings, these power figures are recorded here as this building's own utility service and standby generation, though Csquare does not separately label any of them as IT load, so no IT capacity figure is written.

Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, reports having begun operations in January 2019 under the name BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, a lineage that continued through Evoque Data Center Solutions under Brookfield affiliated ownership, then Centersquare, then Csquare, converting to a Delaware corporation on June 15, 2026 shortly before a July 16, 2026 initial public offering priced at 21 dollars a share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross. Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under New York Stock Exchange rules. As of March 31, 2026 the company's portfolio spanned 64 sites across 21 metro markets in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, and its own prospectus names California, alongside Boston, as a market where power costs run higher and more volatile than the company average. No tenant is named for SFO3 in any source reviewed.

Sunnyvale sits between San Jose and Mountain View in the heart of Silicon Valley, and the Kifer Road corridor near this building has long hosted a mix of enterprise office and light industrial buildings, several converted to data center or telecom use over the decades, consistent with this facility's CenturyLink and Savvis heritage origins and its current leased, rather than owned, status in Csquare's portfolio.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO3 in Sunnyvale publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space. The spec does not break that figure into IT load versus overhead, so the usable compute capacity is not determinable from published data alone. Treating the full 129.4 MW as a rough upper bound on IT load, and assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, the campus could support on the order of 3,200 racks. At the higher densities now common for GPU clusters, 80 to 100 kW per rack, the same power envelope would shrink rack count to roughly 1,300 to 1,600 racks. Power, not floor space, is the binding variable here.

The six certifications qualify this campus to host workloads with specific compliance requirements. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to audited controls over financial reporting and operational security. PCI DSS qualifies the facility for payment card data environments. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for information security management and federal-aligned security frameworks respectively. LEED indicates a rating for energy and environmental design, though the level is not published on the operator's spec page.

Within California, this site ranks eighth by published megawatts among the facilities tracked here, and California has 103 mapped facilities of which only seven publish a megawatt figure at all. The seven facilities with published figures total 185 MW combined, and SFO3's 129.4 MW represents approximately 70 percent of that published total. This concentration reflects how rarely operators publish capacity figures rather than a claim that this campus dominates the state's actual installed base.
